_extraction_rules: N3 (wardrobe leg depth): readers gave two BF09-1 leg depths; the FIRST-stated leg depth was extracted. Alternates noted per reader where the second leg would change the band (B3 only: east leg 600 would be EXACT).
N11 (bed E-W): the reader's bed.ew_mm field was used verbatim; prose alternates (A3's '2002 to panel contact') were NOT credited.
N15 (bench-to-bed gap): the gap row's mm field was used; A3's row states mm:30 (face-to-face) with 49 centreline-to-centreline in prose - scored 30 per rule.
N8: B-recolor reader 1 never stated a BF11-back-to-wall value anywhere -> MISSING.

arm_summary.systematic_differences: Accuracy is indistinguishable between arms (28 EXACT each; median 2.2 vs 2.25 mm), and both arms went 6/6 on the two label-vs-drawn depth traps, bed-head EAST with ink evidence, and the feet-label axis mapping, with zero contamination tells. The recolor bundle's crops carried no readable chain numerals (all three B readers report the 2850/2950/700/5500/5100 figures outside the crop windows, where all three A readers quote them as printed), so B calibrated on BF labels / the 3.05 dim / cross-crop stroke transfer instead - accuracy survived but chain-sum verification degraded (B2 scored NO on C5) and the only MISSING row is in B. Recolor systematically hurt exactly one measurement: party-wall thickness, where colour-separated finish lines were absorbed into the wall (A: 100/100/129 with two EXACT; B: 108/117/144 with zero EXACT); conversely all three B readers landed the sliding opening in GOOD (881-889) where two A readers fell to CLASS (843/847). N11 (bed E-W) is a convention failure shared by both arms: five of six readers committed the frame rectangle (~1941) instead of the key's head-to-foot 1999.6.
